docket.summary: Delta 1696 FLL-ATL, B757-251 N540US. Held ~17 min at FL270 for a microburst alert, then ILS 9R. After main-gear touchdown the PF over-rotated, the airplane lifted off again and struck its tail; the captain flew a go-around and landed on runway 10. Crew never sensed the strike; damage found ~5 h later.
sources: Meteorology Specialist's Factual Report, Sep 29 2022 (ATL 5-min ASOS 2120: A3022)

alerts.why: Pitch 10.6-12.0 deg with the mains on the runway after touchdown; the tail struck here (757-200 contact ~12 deg).

silent.why: Cruise FL370-FL380, VNAV/FL CH step down to FL340: nothing abnormal happened.
Every descent was flown in VNAV or FL CH with the autopilot engaged.
Max recorded CAS ~318 kt vs VMO 350. The 384-kt ground readings are ADC sentinels.
Taxi-in: CAS sentinel at 384 kt must not read as an airspeed failure.
Takeoff rotation and the approach stayed well inside tail clearance.
Second landing on runway 10 was normal.

grace.why: Tail strike on the go-around at ATL: the nearest suitable airport is the one the aircraft is circling, and that is where it landed.

known_false_alarms.cause: Compares against the profile's cruise altitude; ATC-assigned levels (FL370, FL380, FL340) aren't on this FDR frame, so every level change reads as a deviation.
Predictive time-to-VMO extrapolates takeoff-roll and climb acceleration; fires at 93 kt on the runway.
Alerts whenever altitude x L/D is short, engines running or not — every departure and approach.
One VFE (flaps-30, 162 kt) applied to every flap setting; flaps 5-20 placards are much higher.
Static-source position error during rotation moves recorded pressure altitude; the jerk check reads it as a g event.
Layer decided from indicated altitude with no hysteresis: ~300 ft band around 18,000 ft where neither QNH nor STD passes.
Path computed as MSL altitude vs distance to the airport reference point — assumes a sea-level field and ignores ATL's 1,026 ft elevation and the runway threshold.
Raw radio-altitude closure over rolling terrain, no Mode 2B landing-configuration desensitisation.
-500/-800 fpm limits below 1,000 ft RA; a 3-degree ILS at 140 kt groundspeed is ~-750 fpm.
No flare/rollout inhibit: IAS below Vref in the flare and on the landing roll is normal.
Peak radio altitude kept from the original takeoff and only reset in GROUND_ROLL, so the go-around after the bounce reads as a 1,500 ft sink.
Flaps retracted on taxi-in trigger the takeoff-configuration warning.
